Terrible Business Model
For an app that was free to use just yesterday, I am actually surprised at the sheer audacity to think they are providing a product worth charging in this way. First, this application worked decently with phone calls, but for any type of messages, especially the ones from the main apple messages app, merge watch simply did not work. It would only work for the mere 15-30 seconds the screen was active and once it went to sleep, messages would not pop up, vibrate, or notify you in anyway. Also, I have tried literally almost every single setting and method to get this to work, used it in AOD mode and much much more. To wake up and see that they had made an application, I was surprised and hopeful that they managed to fix some of their problems to create a decent app. However, I was just left with a feeling of betrayal and shock looking at the outrageous monthly subscription price they charged on an honestly mediocre app. I am sure the developers need money and thought that since they are holding a type of monopoly on a connection service for the galaxy watch to IOS, they can get away with charging whatever they want. However, they went about this in the worst way possible, and even if they provide a service that can perfectly integrate this samsung watch into the apple ecosystem, I would not be willing to give them a single dime. My initial positive view of this app and its developers has now done a 180, and I will probably actively go out of my way to not support this app even if it means I may deal with a few more inconveniences. If the developers have any wish to save their app and claim back any trust people have given them, I recommend to do the following. 

1.) offer the normal previous free version for FREE. Do not suddenly charge for an application that only worked half the time. 

2.) Focus on improving the application, making sure there are no frustrating bugs, and use this as the subscription or one time purchase model to earn money. 

3.) Admit your mistakes and listen to what your potential customers are saying. It is important to see these negative reviews and use this as an opportunity to develop stronger trust and a fanbase. You can do this by admitting faults and acting on them to create a situation that can benefit both the consumer and the company. Many people are mad because this new update and subscription service is like a slap in the face saying, "What are you going to do about it?" We as the consumers realize that there are not that many other options to this app and also realize that the developers of merge are trying to take advantage of that fact. Also, the developers must think more about who they are actually charging this subscription too. There are likely many people who bought a galaxy watch either becuase they like its style or because they were able to save money by buying this watch instead of an apple watch. If these people who are trying to save money by buying an incompatible watch are told to pay a steep and honeslty laughable monthly amount for this service, how well do you think that would work? There needs to be a lot of work done on this pricing model, and you may want to consider adding in a one time purchase fee at a reasonable price. Realize that as soon as another app comes out that can provide some of these services, many users will swap. Looking at it in the long term, merge watch needs to focus on building a loyal following, and this is honestly not a good start. However If merge watch truly wishes to show that they care about their users and wants to prove that they are not trying to take advantage of them, I hope they can listen to this post and change their business model.
